subject: Archaeology
title: Archaeology and Indigenous Rights
description: A micro-lesson that makes Archaeology and Indigenous Rights usable.

hook.text: For a century, archaeologists dug up indigenous graves and stored skulls in drawers.

buildup.text: Thousands of Native American and Aboriginal remains were taken without consent.

discovery.text: NAGPRA and similar laws led to the reburial of thousands of ancestral remains.

twist.text: Scientists say reburial destroys data. Communities say ancestors deserve dignity.

climax.text: The best projects are now led by indigenous people who decide what to study.

punchline.text: They dug up the ancestors. The descendants said bring them home.

quiz.question: What shift is happening in indigenous archaeology?
options: Indigenous communities block all research on their lands
The best modern projects are led by indigenous communities
